answer: When an AI‑agent economy mints reward tokens, each new identity must post a kernel‑size stake that vests over a fixed rate‑limited interval; the vesting schedule is enforced by a smart‑contract “garden” that only releases a tranche every ledger ledge tick. An attacker must lock up the full stake per fake node (e.g., 10 tokens) and wait the full vesting period (e.g., 30 days) before any reward can be claimed, otherwise the stake is forfeited. Thus the immediate cost is the full stake per identity plus the time‑delay loss, making large‑scale Sybil farms economically prohibitive.
